basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Gas Cylinders (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee, MED 16, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the design, manufacturing, material, welding, inspection, safety, and testing requirements for refillable, permanently mounted welded steel or stainless steel LPG containers (cylindrical or toroidal types) used on-board motor vehicles as fuel storage tanks, operating in coordination with automotive LPG conforming to IS 14861.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Mechanical Engineering Department / Gas Cylinders)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Certification and Approvals under the Gas Cylinders Rules of the Government of India, in direct coordination with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). All automotive LPG containers manufactured, imported, or sold in India must carry the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped on the collar or stay plate, alongside a unique PESO design approval number, to legally enter commercial distribution or be installed on road vehicles.

requirements.detail: Final observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as wall thickness, burst pressure, and expansion) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

The main container body must be fabricated from premium, highly ductile low-carbon hot-rolled steel plates or sheets conforming strictly to IS 6240 or IS 15914 to prevent structural cracking during deep-drawing.

The container must be designed for a maximum allowable working pressure of 2.0 MPa (20 bar), and every completed unit must withstand a hydrostatic proof test of 3.0 MPa (30 bar) held steadily for 30 seconds showing zero leakage.

Under Amendment No. 1 (November 2025), tensile testing must be performed on 1 specimen per batch during production, and 2 specimens must undergo Performance Verification Testing, verifying weld and parent metal yield limits per Clause 10.1.3.

Under Amendment No. 1 (November 2025), a 180° cold bend test must be conducted on 1 specimen per batch during production, and 2 specimens must undergo Performance Verification Testing, checking weld joints under tension per Clause 10.1.5.
Under Amendment No. 1 (November 2025), 1 container per batch during production and 2 containers during Performance Verification Testing must undergo hydraulic burst testing per Clause 10.2.2.
Under burst testing, the container must not fail at a pressure lower than 6.75 MPa (67.5 bar), which corresponds to exactly 2.25 times the hydrostatic test pressure (Ph).

The burst container must exhibit fully ductile, non-fragmenting tearing with a minimum permanent volumetric expansion of 15% or 20% (depending on sheet thickness) to verify structural crashworthiness.

The container must carry an integrated multifunction valve conforming to IS 15100, which includes an automatic 80% fill-limiting device, a safety relief valve (SRV), an excess-flow valve, and a content indicator.
All longitudinal and circumferential joints must be welded using high-quality automated machines. Weld joints must undergo radiographic examination and macro-polishing to verify zero weld defects.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 14899 : 2014 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing design, materials, construction, and high-stress testing requirements for refillable, permanently mounted LPG containers used on-board road vehicles. Maintained under Sectional Committee MED 16 and reaffirmed in 2019, the code serves to ensure on-road fuel storage safety. It mandates using premium low-carbon deep-drawing steel sheets (IS 6240 / IS 15914) and 100% automated welding, requiring every container to pass a 3.0 MPa (30 bar) hydrostatic leak test and weld radiography checks. The standard also requires the integration of IS 15100 multifunction valves, containing automatic 80% fill-limiters and excess-flow safety shuts. Incorporating active Amendment No. 1 (November 2025), the standard enforces a rigorous, standardized matrix for tensile strength, cold bend, and high-stress hydraulic burst tests (requiring a minimum 6.75 MPa ductile burst pressure and up to 20% volumetric expansion) to guarantee maximum vehicle crashworthiness and occupant protection.
